answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can claim rewards, and the protocol caps how much influence one bonded identity can gain during each epoch. A Sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each needs its own locked capital, while splitting influence across them does not bypass the cap. If detected cheating triggers slashing, the attacker loses bonds; honest agents can use quill to record claims, tend the garden of shared tasks, and compare each other’s work for an echo of copied outputs.
